findingsReportedNotFixed.finding: the read route is an existence-and-kind oracle for a private ref the caller already holds but that belongs to another match. Measured: 200 with {opaqueRef, payloadState, recordKind} and an export-attempt/denied audit row. No payload crosses. The shape follows from the service's deliberate non-oracle fallback (ViewerHistoryService.ts:325-331) meeting a route that accepts caller-named refs; closing it would mean a route-level pre-check that reintroduces the very status-code oracle the fallback exists to prevent. Raised rather than guarded, per the charter addendum

branding the host as gm widens the host's OWN view of its own match beyond the private record: GM-class timeline rows (raw committed revision ranges, every actor's principal id) ride the same body. No player's view changes. Narrowing it would need a service-level private-only entrypoint - outside this unit's paths and larger than the route. Pinned by 'brands the host as GM for the whole export, not only the record' so the decision is visible rather than implied

the campaign rewind-preview route under src/pages/api/campaigns writes drafts through the same GmPrivatePreviewRecordWriter and still discards its refs, so a campaign GM has no handle and cannot use this route. Outside this unit's ownership paths; a narrow successor would apply design A there

IPrivateRecordRepository exposes no listing by campaignSessionId (IPrivateRecordRepository.ts:278-292). If it did, the read route could enumerate a match's own gm-drafts for the branded GM and the preview would not have to hand out refs at all - a smaller contract than threading handles through a response body. That is a src/lib/events/privacy change, outside this unit's paths, and it is the shape the owner may prefer long-term

an unknown ref and a denied ref are told apart by the response body (an empty privateRecords array vs a payload-free view), not by status. That is consistent with the non-oracle law but it does mean a caller can distinguish 'no such record' from 'record exists, not yours'. Pinned by two separate rows so the behaviour is explicit
